channel.title: Mathematics on metafunctor
channel.description: Research Engineer & Computer Scientist - Machine Learning, Statistical Computing, Open Source Development

item.title: Reverse-Process Synthetic Data Generation for Math Reasoning
item.dc:creator: admin
item.description: Training LLMs on mathematical reasoning by inverting easy-to-solve problems: generate derivatives, reverse them into integration exercises with full step-by-step solutions.

item.title: Master's Project: Reliability Estimation in Series Systems
item.dc:creator: admin
item.description: My master's project on maximum likelihood estimation for series systems with right-censored and masked failure data.

item.title: Finding Every Smallest C6-Saturated Graph
item.dc:creator: Alexander Richard Towell
item.description: An eleven-vertex witness, 205 minimum graphs on fourteen vertices, and the difference between finding an example and proving a minimum.

item.title: Extremal Graph Witnesses on the House of Graphs
item.dc:creator: admin
item.description: Four extremal graphs deposited to the House of Graphs: a minimum C6-saturated graph and three Zarankiewicz witnesses. Plus two new exact saturation values, verified and prepared for deposit.

item.title: Fifteen Integer Sequences in the OEIS
item.dc:creator: admin
item.description: Fifteen integer sequences now published in the OEIS: nine authored, six extended. Computed by SAT solving and exhaustive search, checked against prior art, spread across seven fields.

item.title: The Expensive Half of a SAT Proof
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: A from-first-principles tour of double-lex symmetry breaking for SAT: why the UNSAT side is expensive, how canonical-representative constraints fix it, a worked Zarankiewicz example that settled three new OEIS values, and an honest map of where the technique stops scaling.

item.title: Synthesis: Codecs as Structure
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: The series closes by restating the codes-as-priors thesis across all twelve instances and connecting the wire-format side to the Stepanov type-algebra side.

item.title: Bits Follow Types
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: Codecs are not ad-hoc bit formats. They are constructions on the algebraic structure of types.

item.title: When Lists Become Bits
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: Prefix-freeness is the property that lifts the free-monoid construction into bit space.

item.title: What Happens When You Let an AI Loose on 1,000 Erdős Problems
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: I pointed Claude Code at the Erdős problem database with vague instructions to 'find interesting things.' It built 92 Python modules, ran 131 subagents, and computed exact Ramsey numbers nobody had computed before. I mostly watched.

item.title: Free Algebras: Why Lists and Polynomials Are Universal
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: The free monoid on a set is the type of lists over that set. The universal property says fold is the unique homomorphism from lists to any monoid. This explains why lists, multisets, and polynomials appear everywhere.

item.title: Homomorphisms: The Maps Between Structures
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: A homomorphism preserves structure. fold is the universal homomorphism from the free monoid. This is the algebraic reason that fold, evaluation, and parallelism work.

item.title: Lattices: Fixed Points and Iteration
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: A lattice has two operations, meet and join, satisfying absorption laws. Tarski's theorem gives a generic fixed-point algorithm. Lattice structure determines the iteration, just as monoid structure determines power-by-squaring.

item.title: Semirings: One Algorithm, Six Graph Problems
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: A semiring has two monoidal operations linked by distributivity. Matrix multiplication over different semirings gives shortest paths, longest paths, widest paths, reachability, and path counting, all from the same code.

item.title: Streaming Statistics, One Monoid at a Time
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: Online accumulators are monoids. Default construction is the identity, combination via += is the binary operation, and parallel composition gives the product monoid, computing arbitrary statistics in a single pass.

item.title: Duality: The Hidden Structure of Opposites
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: Many structures come in pairs: forward/reverse AD, push/pull iteration, encode/decode. Recognizing duality lets you transfer theorems and insights between domains.

item.title: Seeing Structure First
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: A reflection on eleven explorations in generic programming, and how algorithms arise from algebraic structure.

item.title: RoaringBitmap
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: A hybrid compressed bitmap that picks the optimal sub-representation (array, bitmap, or run-length) per 64K-integer chunk based on density. No single prior dominates: Roaring commits to none and adapts per chunk.

item.title: Closed-Form Results for Masked Exponential Series Systems
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: Closed-form MLEs and Fisher information for exponential series systems with masked failure data. No numerical optimization required.

item.title: Choosing the Algebra
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: The Stepanov series showed that algorithms arise from algebraic structure. This post is about the flip side: sometimes you choose a different structure to make the algorithm trivial.
